analysis.design: paired; every arm scores the same file from one reading
analysis.unit: one file, one verdict; a false positive is suspicious: true
analysis.test: exact McNemar, binomial, one-sided, on discordant pairs
analysis.interval: Clopper-Pearson, one-sided, 95%; the upper limit is what is judged
analysis.multiplicity: no adjustment across strata, per the predeclaration

bound_1.statement: False-positive difference on validated formats must be within 2.00 percentage points at the upper limit of a one-sided 95% interval.
bound_1.verdict: Arm C introduces 30 new false positives on 155 validated-format files, an upper limit of 25.3235 pp against a tolerance of 2.0 pp. The bound is NOT met.
bound_1.note_on_other_arms: Every other arm's figure is reported for completeness and none is judged against this bound. Arm D in particular was selected after Arm C's benign cost was measured; presenting its result as meeting a predeclared bound would be choosing the arm after seeing the data.

bound_2.statement: The unvalidated x incompressible false-positive rate may not be so high that this stratum alone would push the corpus-wide rate above Table 5.9's 5%.

d5.rule: D5 - if false positives in the unvalidated x incompressible stratum exceed the predeclared tolerance, do not ship the repair by default. Ship behind an operator switch and state that a real validator for that format is the correct long-term fix.
d5.decision: D5 fires. Arm C raises 90 false positives on 90 files in this stratum - 100.0 pp against a tolerance of 15.0 pp, which it exceeds by a factor of 6.7. The repair does NOT ship by default. It stays behind CONTAINER_EXEMPTION_POLICY, whose default is `legacy`, and the correct long-term fix is a real structural validator for bzip2, xz, GIF and RIFF - which Chapter 9 §9.13 places outside this project's scope.
